Python notebooks can now have **Run in browser** and **Download and run** buttons.
JupyterLite supplies the editor, and Pyodide runs Python in the reader's browser.
The buttons and the loading page use the fonts and colours of your site's theme.

Install `smalldocs[notebooks]` and set `browser-notebooks: true` to turn on the feature.
The build reads imports, checks the Pyodide package disallow list, and puts dependency metadata into a copied notebook.
The source notebook stays unchanged, and the build runs no notebook code.

The documentation includes two examples:

- [A plot in the browser](../guide/browser-plot/index.ipynb) uses NumPy and Matplotlib to draw sine and cosine curves.
- [Read data in the browser](../guide/browser-data/index.ipynb) reads a bundled CSV file with Pandas and draws a Seaborn plot.

The [browser notebook guide](../guide/browser-notebooks.qmd) covers setup, lint, data files and downloads.
Sites that leave the feature off keep their existing output.
